cards.text: Paul is writing to the church of the Thessalonians, along with Silvanus and Timothy (2 Thessalonians 1:1). Now he gets to a BIG one: the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered together to Him. Something's been going around that church, and Paul wants to talk about it.

cards.question: Paul asks the brothers not to be easily alarmed by a message going around about the Lord's coming. What does that message claim?

answers.text: The Day of the Lord has already come
The Day of the Lord will come next spring
The Day of the Lord will never come

cards.text: Paul says not to be alarmed by "any spirit or message or letter seeming to be from us". Friend, that's a text from your boss's number saying the office is closed FOREVER, and half the team already went home without calling to check.

cards.question: True or false: Paul tells the Thessalonians the Day of the Lord might already be here.

cards.text: Paul is clear: "Let no one deceive you in any way". That Day won't come until the rebellion happens and the man of lawlessness, the son of destruction, is revealed.

cards.question: Paul says the man of lawlessness will oppose and exalt himself above every so-called god or object of worship. Who will he proclaim himself to be?
The man of lawlessness puts himself above everything people worship. Where does Paul say he will seat himself?

cards.text: And sitting there, he proclaims himself to be God, which, friend, is a WHOLE lot of nerve. I spent years under a takeout menu in a junk drawer and never once called myself king of the drawer.

cards.question: Paul isn't telling the Thessalonians anything new about the man of lawlessness. Why should they already know it?

answers.text: They read it in the prophets

cards.text: Paul says they know what is restraining the man of lawlessness right now, so that he'll be revealed at the proper time. Paul doesn't spell out what it is here, and neither will I.

cards.question: Something is holding lawlessness back. Paul says the mystery of lawlessness is ___ at work.
Paul says someone is restraining lawlessness right now. How long will he keep at it?

answers.text: Until he is taken out of the way
Until Paul comes back to visit

cards.question: Once the restrainer is out of the way, the lawless one is revealed. True or false: Paul says the Lord Jesus will slay him.

cards.text: All that big talk, and it ends with a breath. The Lord Jesus will slay him with the breath of His mouth and annihilate him by the majesty of His arrival.
Paul says the lawless one's coming will come with the working of Satan, with "every kind of power, sign, and false wonder". Friend, that is one arrival you do NOT want to be impressed by.
Paul says the lawless one also comes with every wicked deception, aimed at those who are perishing.

cards.question: Paul says the people falling for the deception refused the love of the ___ that would have saved them.

cards.text: Paul says that for this reason, God will send them a powerful delusion, so they believe the lie.

cards.question: Paul says judgment will come on everyone who disbelieved the truth. What else did they do?

cards.text: Then the letter turns so hard my mustache needs a seatbelt. Paul says, "But we should always thank God for you, brothers who are loved by the Lord".

cards.question: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians because God chose them to be saved. When did God choose them?

answers.text: On the day they were baptized

cards.question: Others refused the truth. True or false: Paul says God chose the Thessalonians to be saved by the sanctification of the Spirit and by faith in the truth.

cards.text: Paul says God called them to this through the gospel he and his team brought them. And there's a reason for that call.

cards.question: God called the Thessalonians through the gospel. What does Paul say He called them for?

answers.text: To share in the glory of Jesus Christ
To be spared from every trouble
To be honored by every nation

cards.text: Rumors, mystery messages, a lawless one with false wonders. I bet Paul's ready to cut through all that noise, and he gives them something solid to hold on to.

cards.question: With rumors flying about the Day of the Lord, what does Paul tell the brothers to do?

answers.text: Stand firm and hold to what they were taught
Write to Paul before believing anything
Stay home and wait for the Day to come

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the traditions he taught the Thessalonians came to them only by speech.

cards.text: Paul wraps up with a "Now may" for them. It names our Lord Jesus Christ Himself and God our Father, "who by grace has loved us and given us eternal comfort and good hope".

cards.question: True or false: Paul closes by saying may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself and God our Father encourage the Thessalonians' hearts.
Paul's closing words also say may our Lord Jesus Christ and God our Father strengthen the Thessalonians. In what?

findings.problem: This story card only retells what cards 6 and 7 just asked and answered: he sits in the temple and proclaims himself to be God (2 Thessalonians 2:4). It adds a joke but doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells new material, or this card should be cut.

The setup ends with 'he gives them something solid to hold on to.' That points straight at the right answer on card 12, 'Stand firm and hold to what they were taught.' It shares the word 'hold' and rules out 'Write to Paul' and 'Stay home and wait' before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Most of this card ('Rumors, mystery messages, a lawless one with false wonders') recaps verses 2 and 9 instead of moving the passage forward. It cites verse 15 but tells nothing from verse 15.

The card asks the baker to finish the line 'strengthen you in every ___.' The three answers are 'Every good word and deed,' 'Every battle they face' and 'Every journey they take.' Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason to 'good word and deed,' so this is guessing a line's wording, like the anoint-with-oil example. Ask about the meaning or movement of the blessing instead.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'Paul wraps up' (card 14), 'Paul closes by saying' (card 15) and 'Paul's closing words' (card 16) suggest Paul is ending the letter. 2 Thessalonians 3 goes on ('Finally, brothers,' 3:1). Verses 16 and 17 close this section, not the letter. Reword so the cards don't say the letter is ending.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Stop 2's lighter, hopeful turn (verses 13 to 17) has room for real laughs, but most cards are plain retelling (cards 2, 4, 9 and 14). The few jokes are mild ('one arrival you do NOT want to be impressed by'). Cards 2 and 4 cover judgment and can stay serious, but cards 9 and 14 read like a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
